standard_prerequisites.name: Higher cohomology of a quasi-coherent module on an affine open vanishes
standard_prerequisites.use: Verifies the vanishing condition of the suitable-system lemma.

standard_prerequisites.name: On an affine open the sections functor identifies quasi-coherent modules with modules, so a surjective map of modules gives a surjective map on sections
standard_prerequisites.use: Verifies the surjectivity condition of the suitable-system lemma.

standard_prerequisites.name: The derived limit lemma for suitable inverse systems computes H^q(Rlim K_n) as lim H^q(K_n)
The comparison lemma between inverse limits and derived limits of module systems gives parts (2) and (3)

core_obligations: Set B the affine opens of X; for U in B, H^p(U, H^q(K_n)) = 0 because H^q(K_n) is quasi-coherent, and the maps on sections H^0(U, H^q(K_{n+1})) -> H^0(U, H^q(K_n)) are surjective by the schemes equivalence lemma (proof lines 334-340).
Part (1): these two facts verify the hypotheses of the derived-limit suitable-system lemma, which gives H^q(K) = lim H^q(K_n) (proof lines 341-343).
Parts (2) and (3): the inverse-limit comparison lemma gives Rlim H^q(K_n) = lim H^q(K_n) and the vanishing of higher cohomology of the limit on affine opens (proof lines 344-345).
proof_roadmap: Verify the two conditions of the suitable-system lemma on affine opens (proof lines 334-340).
Apply the suitable-system lemma for part (1) (proof lines 341-343).
Apply the inverse-limit comparison for parts (2) and (3) (proof lines 344-345).
